summary.text: A 45-year-old male heavy smoker without significant prior medical history presented to a teaching hospital clinic in Khartoum, Sudan, for reconstruction of mandibular and soft tissue defects caused by a gunshot injury two years earlier. Preoperative volume-rendered 3D CT showed a segmental mandibular continuity defect spanned by a temporary reconstruction plate, and ECG, chest radiograph and anesthesia evaluation were unremarkable, with ASA class II.

Preoperative and postoperative day 5 hematology and coagulation values were tabulated, with a platelet count of 240×10^(9)/L before surgery and 42×10^(9)/L on postoperative day 5. A heparin 5000 IU intravenous bolus was given preoperatively; the operation removed the temporary plate, harvested a left-leg fibular osteocutaneous flap and established arterial and venous anastomoses, and proceeded uneventfully.

Postoperative care included subcutaneous heparin twice daily and hourly flap monitoring. Venous congestion first appeared on postoperative day 3 and persisted despite needle punctures and re-exploration, which found multiple venous anastomotic thrombi treated with mechanical thrombectomy. Congestion recurred, prompting three additional explorations that showed adequate arterial inflow but recurrent venous thrombosis, with only transient improvement.

On postoperative day 5 the platelet count fell to 42×10⁹/L with rapid clinical deterioration. A hematology consultation confirmed heparin-induced thrombocytopenia with thrombosis, the 4Ts score was 8/8, and PF4-heparin ELISA later returned positive. The patient progressed to multiorgan failure and died on postoperative day 7.

ambiguities.issue: The text describes a first re-exploration on the day congestion appeared, with multiple venous anastomotic thrombi, followed by three additional explorations over the subsequent 48 hours; Table 4 (Appendix D) logs four re-explorations on POD 3 and POD 4, the first with multiple intraluminal venous thrombi. The counts and findings are consistent, but the source does not literally map each text exploration to a table row, so text and table items are kept separate. The Table 4 legend says times are in 24-hour format, yet the rows give only day-part labels.
